“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).

These are the words Joseph heard from the mouth of the angel who was telling him to marry Mary. This direction and promise of salvation from sins gave Joseph assurance where he had doubts before.

These same words have assured many people through the ages that their sins were forgiven through Jesus.

The problem is that these words and similar salvation promises are often taken out of the larger gospel context. They are misquoted to assure people of eternal salvation in the context of partial obedience or even outright sin.

There were two conditions that qualified and energized the salvation that Jesus brought. These conditions must still be met today if we are to find our names written in the Lamb’s book of life.

The first condition is that we must be willing to own our sins, including our sinful nature, in humble, honest repentance and confession.

Many of the Pharisees did not want to acknowledge their sinful state. Here are some verses in John 3:18-21 that help us grasp this obstacle. “And men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God” (John 3:19-21).

In a performance-based culture, it is humiliating to acknowledge sinful acts or habitual practices. It is tempting to admit mistakes with vague acknowledgments such as “I haven’t always done as I should have.” Owning our sins is the very narrow gate that all who want to be a part of the kingdom of heaven must enter.

In a sense, the publicans and harlots had a lower hurdle for entering the kingdom of heaven. These people already knew about their sins. They readily acknowledged their needs, opening their hearts to Jesus’ ongoing gospel message. “And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John. But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him” (Luke 7:29-30).

The more difficult challenge came to those who had carefully hidden their sins. We all have sins, but some are open and may be sent beforehand to judgment. The hidden ones cannot be forgiven and will meet the sinner at his final judgment. “Some men’s sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after. Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid” (1 Timothy 5:24-25).

The second condition is that we must be willing to turn away from the practice of our sins. Jesus gives this condition as a requirement to receive forgiveness.

This may be discerned in a few of His directives to penitent sinners:

  • “And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more” (John 8:11).
  • “Go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me” (Mark 10:21).
  • “When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren” (Luke 22:32).
  • “And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it” (Luke 9:23-24).

Today, the popular version of the gospel is that when a person believes in Christ, he is forgiven of all his past, present, and future sins. Divorced and remarried couples are assured they may stay in that state. Those living extravagant or selfish lifestyles are assured of a loving heavenly Father. Christians supposedly live as sinners; they just live without any guilt! Really?

Will John the Baptist need to apologize to Herod for not offering to take him to Jesus so he could be forgiven and remain with Herodias? (Read Mark 6:16-28.) Did he have to be so confrontational and thereby lose his head?

No, Jesus came to save people from their past sins and their sinful/selfish lifestyles. Let us not compromise His message and experience the torments of an eternity without the gospel. Instead, let us be faithful to the cross-bearing that Jesus taught so we can be partakers with the truly redeemed in eternity. Let us also be brothers to others in cross-bearing, helping them live a life of Christian obedience, truly free from both past and present sins.

“En sy sal ’n seun baar, en jy moet Hom Jesus noem, want dit is Hy wat sy volk van hulle sondes sal verlos” (Matteus 1:21).

Dit is die woorde wat Josef gehoor het uit die mond van die engel wat hom aangesê het om met Maria te trou. Hierdie opdrag en belofte van verlossing van sondes het Josef gerusstelling gegee waar hy voorheen getwyfel het.

Hierdie selfde woorde het deur die eeue heen baie mense die versekering gegee dat hulle sondes deur Jesus vergewe is.

Die probleem is dat hierdie woorde en soortgelyke beloftes van verlossing dikwels buite die groter evangeliekonteks aangehaal word. Hulle word verkeerd aangehaal om mense die versekering van ewige verlossing te gee in die konteks van gedeeltelike gehoorsaamheid of selfs openlike sonde.

Daar was twee voorwaardes wat die verlossing wat Jesus gebring het, moontlik gemaak en krag gegee het. Hierdie voorwaardes moet vandag steeds nagekom word as ons wil hê dat ons name in die Lam se boek van die lewe geskryf moet staan.

Die eerste voorwaarde is dat ons bereid moet wees om ons sondes, insluitend ons sondige natuur, in nederige en eerlike berou en belydenis te erken.

Baie van die Fariseërs wou nie hulle sondige toestand erken nie. Hier is enkele verse in Johannes 3:18-21 wat ons help om hierdie struikelblok te begryp. “En die mense het die duisternis liewer gehad as die lig, omdat hulle werke boos was. Want elkeen wat kwaad doen, haat die lig en kom nie na die lig nie, sodat sy werke nie bestraf word nie. Maar hy wat die waarheid doen, kom na die lig, sodat dit openbaar kan word dat sy werke in God gedoen is” (Johannes 3:19-21).

In ’n kultuur wat op prestasie gebaseer is, is dit vernederend om sondige dade of gewoontes te erken. Dit is aanloklik om foute te erken met vae erkennings soos “Ek het nie altyd gedoen wat ek moes nie.” Om ons sondes te erken, is juis die baie nou poort waardeur almal wat deel wil wees van die koninkryk van die hemel moet ingaan.

In ’n sekere sin het die tollenaars en prostitute ’n laer hindernis gehad om die koninkryk van die hemel binne te gaan. Hierdie mense het reeds van hulle sondes geweet. Hulle het geredelik hulle behoeftes erken en hulle harte vir Jesus se voortgaande evangelieboodskap oopgemaak. “En al die volk wat dit gehoor het, en ook die tollenaars, het God geregverdig deur met die doop van Johannes gedoop te word. Maar die Fariseërs en die wetgeleerdes het die raad van God teen hulleself verwerp, omdat hulle nie deur hom gedoop is nie” (Lukas 7:29-30).

Die moeiliker uitdaging het gekom vir dié wat hulle sondes sorgvuldig weggesteek het. Ons het almal sondes, maar sommige is openlik en kan vooraf na die oordeel gaan. Die verborge sondes kan nie vergewe word nie en sal die sondaar by sy finale oordeel inhaal. “Die sondes van sommige mense is vooraf openbaar en gaan hulle vooruit na die oordeel; maar by ander volg dit agterna. Net so is ook die goeie werke van sommige vooraf openbaar; en dié wat anders is, kan nie verborge bly nie” (1 Timoteus 5:24-25).

Die tweede voorwaarde is dat ons bereid moet wees om op te hou om ons sondes te beoefen. Jesus stel hierdie voorwaarde as ’n vereiste om vergifnis te ontvang.

Dit kan gesien word in enkele van sy opdragte aan berouvolle sondaars:

  • “En Jesus sê vir haar: Ek veroordeel jou ook nie. Gaan heen en sondig nie meer nie” (Johannes 8:11).
  • “Gaan heen, verkoop alles wat jy het, en gee dit aan die armes, en jy sal ’n skat in die hemel hê; kom dan, neem die kruis op en volg My” (Markus 10:21).
  • “En wanneer jy eendag bekeerd is, moet jy jou broeders versterk” (Lukas 22:32).
  • “En Hy sê vir almal: As iemand agter My aan wil kom, moet hy homself verloën en elke dag sy kruis opneem en My volg. Want elkeen wat sy lewe wil red, sal dit verloor; maar elkeen wat sy lewe om My ontwil verloor, hy sal dit red” (Lukas 9:23-24).

Vandag is die gewilde weergawe van die evangelie dat wanneer iemand in Christus glo, al sy sondes uit die verlede, hede en toekoms vergewe is. Geskeide en hertroude paartjies word verseker dat hulle in daardie toestand mag bly. Mense wat ’n uitspattige of selfsugtige lewenstyl volg, word verseker van ’n liefdevolle hemelse Vader. Christene leef kwansuis as sondaars; hulle leef net sonder enige skuldgevoel! Regtig?

Sal Johannes die Doper vir Herodes om verskoning moet vra omdat hy nie aangebied het om hom na Jesus te neem sodat hy vergewe kon word en by Herodias kon bly nie? (Lees Markus 6:16-28.) Moes hy regtig so konfronterend wees en daardeur sy kop verloor?

Nee, Jesus het gekom om mense van hulle sondes uit die verlede en hulle sondige/selfsugtige lewenstyle te verlos. Laat ons nie sy boodskap verwater en die folteringe van ’n ewigheid sonder die evangelie ondervind nie. Laat ons eerder getrou wees aan die kruis wat Jesus ons geleer het om te dra, sodat ons in die ewigheid saam met die waarlik verlostes deel kan hê. Laat ons ook vir ander broers wees in die dra van die kruis en hulle help om ’n lewe van Christelike gehoorsaamheid te lei, waarlik vry van sondes uit die verlede sowel as die hede.
